title: 5.3.9 Lab: Lose, and start again
description: Give the game an end: a flag for playing or over, a losing condition when the ball falls past the bottom, and a restart that puts the score back as well as the ball.

steps.title: Give the game a state
steps.instructions: Add a flag variable that says whether the game is being played, starting at `true`. Put it next to `score` so it is created once, not every frame.
hints: `let playing = true;` — declared outside `draw()` so it survives between frames, like `wasTouching`.

steps.title: End the round
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, when the ball has fallen past the bottom of the canvas, set the flag to `false`. Nothing visible happens yet — the next step is what uses the flag.
hints: `ball.y > 400` is true once the ball is below a 400-tall canvas.
Do not delete the ball; it has to be there when the round restarts.

steps.title: Show the end, then start again
steps.instructions: When the flag is false, draw 'Game over' and the final score instead of the play area. When R is pressed, set the flag back to `true` **and** put the score back to 0.
hints: One `if (playing) { ... } else { ... }` at the top of `draw()` is enough.
Restarting means everything the first frame had: position, velocity, score, and the flag.

requirements.title: A flag says whether the game is being played
requirements.description: A variable created once and starting true is the game's state. Help: 5.3.8 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: The ball falling past the bottom ends the round
requirements.description: Losing is a position test: when the ball's y is past the bottom of the canvas, the round ends. Help: 5.3.8 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: A restart puts the score back
requirements.description: Pressing R starts a fresh round, so the score returns to 0 along with the ball. Help: 5.3.8 (Reading: The state of the game)
